## Question 1 (11a — Continuous Moderation)

Using the `affairs` dataset, fit a linear model predicting marital `satisfaction` from `yearsmarried`, `education`, and their interaction.

a) Report the estimated interaction coefficient and whether it is significant. In your own words, describe what this coefficient says about how the relationship between `yearsmarried` and `satisfaction` changes as `education` increases.{{< hp glyph="b" >}}

b) Explain why the `yearsmarried` coefficient in this model should **not** be described as "the effect of `yearsmarried`."{{< hp glyph="b" >}} What value of `education` does it correspond to, and is that value plausible for anyone in this dataset?


## Question 2 (11a — Interaction Patterns)

Using the `affairs` dataset, fit a linear model predicting `satisfaction` from `yearsmarried`, `education`, and their interaction.

a) Use `estimate_relation()` to plot the model's predictions with `yearsmarried` on the x-axis, spotlighting `education` at the mean and one SD above and below (use `"education=[sd]"` as the second term in `by`). Include the plot in your document.

b) Using your plot, classify this interaction as potentiation, attenuation, or crossover, and justify your choice in two or three sentences.{{< hp glyph="b" >}}


## Question 3 (11a — Centering with Interactions)

Using the `affairs` dataset, fit the model predicting `satisfaction` from `yearsmarried`, `education`, and their interaction **twice**: once with the raw predictors, and once with both predictors centered.

a) Show the coefficients from both models. Which coefficients changed and which stayed essentially the same?

b) Explain why centering changed the coefficients that it did.{{< hp glyph="b" >}} In the centered model, what does the `yearsmarried` coefficient now represent?


## Question 4 (11b — Binary-by-Continuous)

Using the `affairs` dataset, fit a linear model predicting `satisfaction` from `yearsmarried`, `gender`, and their interaction.

a) Report the estimated interaction coefficient and whether it is significant. Which gender shows the steeper relationship between `yearsmarried` and `satisfaction`?

b) Use `estimate_slopes()` to report the slope of `yearsmarried` separately for women and men. Is each slope significantly different from zero, and does that match your answer to Q4a?{{< hp glyph="b" >}}


## Question 5 (11b — Categorical-by-Categorical)

Using the `affairs` dataset, fit a linear model predicting `satisfaction` from `children`, `gender`, and their interaction.

a) Use `estimate_means()` to report the predicted mean `satisfaction` for all four combinations of `children` and `gender`.

b) Report the estimated interaction coefficient and whether it is significant. Is the satisfaction difference between those with and without children the same size for women and men?{{< hp glyph="b" >}}


## Question 6 (11b — Probing a Categorical Interaction)

Using the `affairs` dataset, fit a linear model predicting `satisfaction` from `yearsmarried`, `children`, and their interaction.

a) Use `estimate_relation()` to plot the model's predictions, and use `estimate_slopes()` to report the slope of `yearsmarried` separately for participants with and without children.

b) Based on the interaction test and the two simple slopes, does having children meaningfully moderate the relationship between `yearsmarried` and `satisfaction`?{{< hp glyph="b" >}} Note that "no" can be the correct answer — justify whichever conclusion you reach.
